title: Mitä and ketä in object questions
summary: When the verb calls for partitive, ask mitä (“what”) about a thing or substance and ketä (“who”) about one person: Mitä juot? — What are you drinking? Ketä odotat? — Who are you waiting for? Put the question word first.
targetSkills: Mitä and ketä in object questions
objectives: Choose mitä or ketä in familiar partitive object questions.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose mitä or ketä in familiar partitive object questions.
The question word takes the grammatical place of the missing object. The supplied verb pattern calls for partitive. Use mitä for the thing or substance and ketä for one person.
The question word comes first in these neutral written questions. This lesson does not teach the whole Finnish question-word system or plural-person keitä.
keyPoints: In these partitive object questions, mitä asks about a thing or substance and ketä asks about one person. The verb pattern is supplied.

steps: In these partitive object questions, mitä asks about a thing or substance and ketä asks about one person. The verb pattern is supplied.
Mitä means “what” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of mikä is mitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
juot means “you drink” and works as the verb. juot comes from juoda: juo- + -t.
In these partitive object questions, mitä asks about a thing or substance and ketä asks about one person. The verb pattern is supplied.
Ketä means “who” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of kuka is ketä; learn this pronoun form directly.
odotat means “you are waiting for” and works as the verb. odotat comes from odottaa: odota- + -t, with tt → t.
